title: Melting Face Emoji 🫠 Meaning: Dread, Heat and Cringe
description: The melting face emoji 🫠 is a smile dissolving into a puddle. It covers embarrassment, burnout, quiet dread and literal heat. Here's how people use it.
summary: The 🫠 melting face is a smiling face sinking into a puddle. It means the sender is overwhelmed, mortified, or worn down while still trying to look okay. It is also used literally for hot weather and, more sweetly, for melting with affection after a kind message.
meaning: Imagine keeping a pleasant expression while slowly sliding under the table. That is 🫠. The smile stays fixed as the face loses its shape, which makes it a perfect picture of composure failing. People use it for embarrassment so strong they want to disappear, as in “I called my teacher Mom 🫠,” and for the slow dread of an inbox, a deadline, or a week that will not end.

It arrived in 2021 and found its audience fast, partly because of timing. Its mix of politeness and collapse matched how many people talked about burnout and stress online. It gives a face to “I'm fine” when the speaker is visibly not, in a way that is funny instead of alarming. The tone is self-aware: the sender knows they are being dramatic.

The literal meaning is heat. During heat waves, in stuffy offices, and on summer commutes, 🫠 says the sender is melting. Weather posts and vacation captions use it constantly. This sense needs no interpretation, and it is the one use that works with any audience. Parents at a July soccer tournament and commuters on a packed train with no air conditioning reach for it for the same reason.

There is a softer meaning too. “You remembered my order 🫠” means the sender has turned to mush from affection or flattery. Here the melt is pleasant, close to swooning. The emoji can also carry sarcasm, where the drooping smile stands for forced cheer giving way, as in “another all-hands at 8am 🫠.” Context sorts these out easily in practice.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: Friends use it to share small humiliations and long days. It asks for sympathy without sounding like a cry for help. It also answers compliments and cute messages when the sender feels flustered. Because it holds several meanings at once, it suits moments that are funny, awful, and sweet together.

contexts.label: At work
contexts.body: Common in team chats as shorthand for overload: too many meetings, a system outage, a request that arrives at 4:55. Colleagues read it as honest but good-humored. It is best kept among peers. Sent to a manager about an assignment, it might look like a complaint you have not put into words.

contexts.label: On TikTok and Instagram
contexts.body: Appears under cringe content, secondhand embarrassment, and “me pretending everything is okay” jokes. It also labels summer posts and overheated festival photos. Younger users treat it as a core emoji for feeling socially wrecked, alongside the skull and the face holding back tears.

contexts.label: From a crush
contexts.body: Good news more often than not. Replying 🫠 to a compliment or a thoughtful gesture means it got to them and they are a bit flustered. If it follows an awkward moment between you, it means they are embarrassed, which also suggests they care how they came across.

examples.text: It's 104 degrees and the AC just died 🫠
Waved at someone who was waving at the person behind me 🫠

examples.meaning: Drained and overwhelmed but coping with humor.

examples.text: You saved me the last one?? 🫠
examples.meaning: Touched and flustered by a kind gesture.

examples.text: Just reread the email I sent last night 🫠
Sure, I can take on one more project 🫠

combos.meaning: Completely overwhelmed; the day has defeated the sender.
Melting from sweetness; emotional in a good way.
Saying “all good” while clearly falling apart.

confusedWith.difference: 🙃 is dry sarcasm about a situation, with the sender still intact. 🫠 shows the sender coming apart because of it. Choose 🙃 for irony and 🫠 when embarrassment or exhaustion is the main feeling.
🥵 is a red, sweating, panting face for extreme heat, spicy food, or finding someone attractive. 🫠 also covers heat but adds resignation, and it has no flirtatious sense of someone being “hot.”
🥲 smiles with a single tear and expresses bittersweet or brave-face sadness. 🫠 is less about sorrow and more about being overwhelmed or mortified. Both keep a smile on, for different reasons.

avoid: Don't use it to tell someone you are seriously struggling; its joking tone can hide a real need for help.
Avoid sending it to a boss or client in response to a request, where it may read as reluctance.
Skip it with people unfamiliar with newer emojis, who may not know what the puddle means.
design: A yellow smiling face whose lower half is collapsing into a flat puddle, with the eyes and mouth sliding out of alignment. The smile remains, usually a little lopsided. Apple, Google, Samsung, and Microsoft all show the same idea; they differ in how far the melt has progressed and which way the face slumps. The concept was proposed to Unicode with both literal heat and metaphorical embarrassment in mind.

faqs.a: Mostly it describes uncomfortable feelings such as embarrassment, dread, and exhaustion, but in a humorous, self-aware way. It can also be positive, meaning the sender is melting from affection. It is rarely hostile toward the reader.

faqs.q: What does 🫠 mean from a guy or a girl?
faqs.a: After a compliment or kind act, it means they are flattered to the point of mush. After an awkward exchange, it means they are embarrassed. After talk of work or school, it means they are worn out. It is not specific to any gender.
Both say “I'm fine” with irony. 🙃 is cooler and more sarcastic. 🫠 is more vulnerable, showing someone losing their composure. Many people use 🙃 for annoyance and 🫠 for cringe or overwhelm.

faqs.q: When did the melting face emoji come out?
faqs.a: It was approved in 2021 as part of Emoji 14.0 and reached most phones during the following year. It quickly became one of the most popular faces from that release.

faqs.q: Can 🫠 mean someone is hot or attractive?
faqs.a: Only loosely. It can mean “you make me melt,” which is about the sender's reaction. It is not the usual emoji for calling someone attractive; 🥵 and 🔥 fill that role.
